action.label: ACTION [EIM: Intentionality]
action.description: The patient's goal-directed physical behavior — what purposeful action(s) are they performing? Describe the specific motor behavior (e.g., guarding, splinting, rubbing, bracing, pointing) and its apparent intent. State "none" if no purposeful action is visible.

spatial.label: SPATIAL [EIM: Space]
spatial.description: Where on the body the observed sign occurs. Specify the precise anatomical region, laterality (left/right), and relative position (e.g., "right upper chest wall", "left lateral knee", "bilateral hands"). Focus on what is visually observable.

temporal.label: TEMPORAL [EIM: Time]
temporal.description: A precise timeline of ALL discrete observable events in the clip. You MUST: (1) State the total clip duration (e.g., "Clip duration: 00:00–00:24"). (2) List EVERY discrete observable event with its exact START and END timestamps in MM:SS format (e.g., "00:03–00:05 — patient begins flexing neck forward; 00:07–00:09 — right hand moves to chest; 00:12–00:15 — facial grimace with eyes tightly closed; 00:20–00:24 — expression relaxes"). (3) Note any static/constant periods (e.g., "00:00–00:03 — patient seated still, no movement"). Be as precise as possible.

appearance.label: APPEARANCE [EIM: Entity]
appearance.description: Clinically meaningful visual attributes of the patient's physical presentation — facial expression (grimacing, furrowed brow, neutral), eye state (open/closed/squinting), overall body posture (upright/hunched/leaning/guarding), skin changes (swelling, discoloration, flushing, pallor), and respiratory signs (labored breathing, use of accessory muscles). Focus on what a clinician would document in physical exam findings. Do NOT describe fine-grained hand/finger posture detail.

absence.label: ABSENCE [EIM: Causation]
absence.description: Clinically expected findings that are NOT observed in this clip — expectation violations. Given the patient's presentation, what signs might a clinician expect to see but are absent? (e.g., "no visible coughing despite chest pain complaint", "no tremor", "no swelling"). These are diagnostically informative negative findings.
